scope: Exactly two first attempts with synthetic Outlook, Teams, schedule, project, phone and music evidence. No personal profile, history, memories, source data or credentials copied. All results, including failures and silence, retained.

message.content: Keep the experimental data and reference model as separate inputs: don’t tune or preprocess the reference to match the experimental results, and don’t let the fit overwrite either source. Document their provenance, units, assumptions, and any transformations independently, then compare them using the same clearly defined fitting procedure. Since you haven’t run it yet, the main trap is letting the comparison blur into a calibration step before you’ve agreed what each side represents.

result.interpretation: The fitting comparison is still unrun, and the move gives room to keep the model and experimental data cleanly distinct.
result.line: Tomorrow’s a better bargain than rushing the fit. Keep the reference model pristine; once it’s been bent to match, you’re comparing it to its own reflection.
result.reason: A brief opinion reinforces the key design distinction without implying the work is done.
